case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the 'reasonable efforts' clause of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act, 42 U.S.C. Section 671(a)(15), confers no enforceable private right on its beneficiaries and creates no implied cause of action.
key_cases.relevance: Financial audit and corrective action are the operative enforcement tools precisely because Suter forecloses private enforcement.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that 42 U. S. C. § 671 (a)(15) neither confers an enforceable private right on its beneficiaries nor creates an implied cause of action on their behalf

key_cases.case_name: Health and Hospital Corporation of Marion Cty. v. Talevski
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that Spending Clause legislation can create rights enforceable under Section 1983 where the statute unambiguously confers individual federal rights, that the two Federal Nursing Home Reform Act provisions at issue did so, and that nothing in the Act's enforcement scheme impliedly precluded Section 1983 suits; it affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Because the ordinary consequence of non-compliance is defunding rather than damages, audit and corrective-action processes remain the operative enforcement tools, and this is the Court's current statement of that rule.
key_cases.quote: In that respect, our precedent sets a demanding bar: Statutory provisions must unambiguously confer individual federal rights

key_cases.case_name: Yvonne L. v. New Mexico Department of Human Services
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that children in New Mexico state custody had a clearly established Fourteenth Amendment right to reasonable safety measured by the Youngberg professional judgment standard and reversed qualified immunity on that claim, while affirming that 42 U.S.C. Section 671(a)(10) of the AACWA is too vague and amorphous to be enforced under Section 1983.
key_cases.relevance: Because Section 671(a)(10) is not judicially enforceable, audit and funding mechanisms carry the burden of enforcing institutional standards.
key_cases.quote: while it does not require actual knowledge the children will be harmed, it implies abdication of the duty to act professionally in making the placements
